dedupe_keys.name: nilim technical note 510 critical infrastructure interdependency models and earthquake damage spreading simulation for the tokyo metropolitan area 2009

description: This technical note from Japan's National Institute for Land and Infrastructure Management models how earthquake damage spreads between critical infrastructures and on to social and economic activity, with a case study of an earthquake directly beneath the Tokyo metropolitan area. Shojiro Kataoka, Mai Tsuruta and Yasuhiro Shoji of the institute's earthquake disaster prevention division published it in February 2009 as Technical Note No. 510. They surveyed cases of damage spreading between infrastructures in past earthquakes, organised them as tables and influence diagrams, and built two models of the interdependency structure, one based on a matrix equation and one on system dynamics, which they then used to simulate damage spreading in the capital region. Coverage is the Tokyo metropolitan area, with lessons drawn from earlier Japanese earthquakes. Format and access: a 170-page Japanese PDF with an English title and synopsis, free from the NILIM site. Licence: not stated. Caveats: the models are documented in the report, not released as software, and reflect infrastructure conditions before 2009. It supports cascading failure and hazard exposure studies of lifeline interdependency in large earthquakes. Related catalogue records are the Nankai Trough lifeline countermeasures material and the San Francisco Lifelines Council interdependency study.
